bugs.title: Alarm relay never held for the required 300 ms and can latch on isolated spikes
bugs.description: evaluate() only resets highRun in the c <= CLEAR_C branch (lines 44-48); a sample in the dead band between 8.0 and 12.0 °C leaves highRun untouched, so separated 1-sample spikes accumulate to 3 and latch the alarm, measured as 'pulse from 1.30 s was still on after 2699 ms'. Also setAlarm() (lines 24-28) drives D10 directly with no hold timer, so the relay follows each sample and pulses last only one sample period, measured as 'pulse from 1.04 s lasted 40 ms' and 'pulse from 1.20 s lasted 20 ms' instead of 300 ms. 2 of 2 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 1.04 s lasted 40 ms, expected 300 ± 150 ms.

bugs.title: Settle filter can be starved by repeated short glitches, missing genuine presses
bugs.description: In scanStart() the debounce timer rawChangedAt is reset on every raw level change (lines 41-45), and the press is only accepted once the level has been stable for SETTLE_MS (line 46). bugs.title: Settle filter rejects a valid 13 ms press at the acceptance boundary
bugs.description: The debounce in scanTrigger() only accepts a level once it has been stable for SETTLE_MS (12 ms), measured from rawChangedAt, which is stamped when the change is first observed in loop() (lines 41-46). Because loop() polls asynchronously, a press lasting just over 12 ms can be sampled late and the stability window expires only after the button has already been released, so no burst is started; the measured evidence shows "D8 missed 1 of 3 trigger(s): D8 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 1.00 s" for the 13 ms glitch case. The filter therefore has no margin over the 8 ms bounce spec and drops legitimate presses near the boundary. D8 missed 1 of 3 trigger(s): D8 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 1.00 s.

bugs.title: Mode switch changes extend the stair light timer
bugs.description: onModeChange() calls armTimer() whenever the light is lit (lines 40-43), which resets litSince and restarts the 3000 ms window on every D3 edge. The spec requires D3 to have no effect on D9, but the measured pulse from 517 ms lasted 5483 ms instead of 3000 ± 150 ms, and a bouncing switch produced a 4787 ms pulse. The mode-change handling must not touch the light timer. 1 of 1 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 517 ms lasted 5483 ms, expected 3000 ± 150 ms.

bugs.title: Relay pulse length and start timing wrong
bugs.description: The run is scheduled from the moment startRun() executes (line 30 sets nextRunAt = now + CYCLE_MS), and stopRunAt is computed from that same now (line 29), but the loop only checks `now >= stopRunAt` (line 64) and `now >= nextRunAt` (line 69) with 16-bit millis() values (line 16), so the pulse is cut short and runs drift. Measured evidence shows pulses lasting 201 ms and 500 ms instead of 2000 ± 150 ms, and D6 missing 10 of 13 triggers. The 16-bit wrap in tickNow() also breaks the comparisons, so the first run does not reliably start 5000 ms after power-up. D6 missed 10 of 13 trigger(s): D6 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 952 ms. 8 of 8 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 5.00 s lasted 201 ms, expected 2000 ± 150 ms.

bugs.title: Serial 'mix <n>' not printed once per 5000 ms
bugs.description: announceRun() is only called from startRun() (line 31), which is gated by the 16-bit wrap-prone comparison at line 69 and by nextRunAt being reset to now + CYCLE_MS at line 30 rather than a fixed schedule. Measured evidence shows 98 of 100 intervals out of tolerance with gaps of 2001 ms, 2000 ms and 8 ms, and one scenario with no matching line at all in 4.65 s. The schedule therefore does not hold the required 5000 ± 250 ms period. Expected /^mix [0-9]+$/ every 5000 ± 250 ms; 98 of 100 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 4927 ms.

bugs.title: Relay toggles more than twice per 5000 ms window
bugs.description: drive() (lines 46-47) recomputes the relay state from `running && !held()` on every loop pass with no debounce or edge latching, so each bounce or chatter on D3 toggles D6 immediately. Measured evidence shows 16, 22 and 7 toggles in a 5000 ms window against a limit of 2. The lack of any hysteresis or minimum-state-time in drive() lets contact bounce propagate straight to the relay. D6 toggled 16 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 5.00 s (limit 2), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.
